calls.title: Contextual Bandit Meeting
calls.summary: The team discussed the implementation of contextual bandit queries, agreeing to treat all attributes as categorical in version 1 to streamline UI input. Teresa highlighted the need for validation logic to ensure attributes are pre-specified in the SDK and validated before query use. Luke emphasized the importance of this validation for maintaining query integrity. To enhance UI flow, a checkbox will be added to identify contextual bandit queries, enabling clearer attribute selection. The group decided to store contextual bandit queries with exposure queries to minimize system complexity. A phased integration approach was planned, focusing first on backend persistence and validation before further updates. Key technical changes were outlined to save contextual bandit queries correctly, and regular syncs were established to ensure smooth progress and timely delivery.
calls.keywords: Contextual Bandit, EAQ, Validation, UI Integration, Backend Persistence, Feature Flag

calls.title: Contextual Bandit Meeting
calls.summary: The meeting addressed the current status of the contextual bandit feature, which is functional but requires API and UI improvements before its launch. Luke Smith outlined the progress made with backend data in BigQuery, noting challenges with large datasets in the UI. Teresa Yung highlighted ongoing SDK changes necessary for launch, and the team agreed to combine API and SDK updates into a single pull request for efficiency. The feature will initially be gated behind the Enterprise plan, with stringent licensing controls to prevent unauthorized access. Gaps in feature flag linkage and visual editor support were identified as critical issues for integration. The feature is designed to work with Managed Warehouse for simpler data queries, and the initial UI will be a minimal beta version to support launch efforts, with further improvements planned for future phases.
calls.keywords: Contextual Bandits, Feature Flags, Enterprise Folder, SDK Payload, Managed Warehouse, Visual Editor

calls.title: Contextual Bandit Meeting
calls.summary: The team addressed the setup of contextual bandits, emphasizing the necessity for manual, attribute-driven configurations to ensure accurate targeting via SQL queries. They discussed the importance of linking predefined attributes to prevent misalignment errors and proposed using dropdown selectors to simplify selections. Current designs separate contextual from standard bandits, with plans for eventual unification but managing complexity in the initial phase. User experience challenges were identified, particularly with empty states and flow improvements. Managed Warehouse customers benefit from simplified setups, and future enhancements will focus on clearer UI for attribute selection and scalability for variations. The team emphasized an iterative approach, incorporating user feedback and emphasizing documentation improvements.
calls.keywords: Contextual Bandits, Assignment Query, Attribute Validation, Measurement Arm, Heat Map Results, User Interface

calls.title: Contextual Bandit Meeting
calls.summary: The team discussed the architecture and data interactions within the contextual bandit system, emphasizing the need to separate experiment logic from bandits for enhanced clarity. Key topics included the snapshot creation process managed by the query runner, handling the persistence of contextual bandit events, and simplifying the data model by removing unused experiment fields. Challenges related to event updates, which may be lost if jobs fail, were also acknowledged. The meeting highlighted significant technical decisions regarding code dependencies and the review process for incremental improvements. Participants committed to refining permissions and discussed collaboration methods to ensure smooth progress on the project.
calls.keywords: contextual bandit, experiment architecture, snapshot management, query runner, permissions model, cron job

calls.title: Contextual Bandit Meeting - UI
calls.summary: The team convened to discuss key improvements for the contextual bandit project, emphasizing a unified UI design that aligns with existing experiment pages for increased clarity. They decided to simplify terminology by renaming settings to 'conversion window' to enhance intuitiveness. Progress on backend decoupling was shared, with a focus on code quality during forthcoming reviews. The API strategy was outlined to prioritize essential endpoints for initial release, postponing less critical features. The urgency for a stable beta launch was highlighted amidst competitive pressures, especially in light of market shifts exemplified by recent layoffs at Quizlet, which could affect client focus and business strategy.
calls.keywords: Contextual Bandits, UI Design, Conversion Window, API Endpoints, Beta Launch, Experiment Results
